h1: Wimberley, TX land clearing that keeps the trees
lede: 9 Arrow Land Service does land clearing in Wimberley, TX with a light hand. On Wimberley property, the job is usually clearing brush and cedar while protecting the oaks, the creek trees and the views.

answer.q: How do you clear land in Wimberley, TX without losing the good trees?
answer.a: Land clearing in Wimberley, TX keeps the good trees through selective forestry mulching. 9 Arrow Land Service picks out cedar, brush and dead wood and grinds them in place, working around the live oaks and the trees along the creeks. Root balls and soil stay put, which matters on Wimberley slopes.

sections.h2: Cypress Creek, the Blanco River and the hills between
paras: Wimberley is in western Hays County on RR 12, northwest of San Marcos, where Cypress Creek meets the Blanco River. Bald cypress and pecan line the creek banks. Above them, cedar, oak and grasses grow in shallow clay loams on the slopes and benches.

Wimberley property tends to sit somewhere on those slopes, between the water and the ridge. A lot cleared bare would lose its shade, its views and the roots holding the hillside together, so land clearing in Wimberley leans selective.
FM 2325 leads northwest toward [land clearing in Blanco](land-clearing-blanco-tx), and the Comal County hills around [land clearing in Canyon Lake](land-clearing-canyon-lake-tx) lie to the southwest.

sections.h2: Selective land clearing in Wimberley, tree by tree
paras: Compact track machines fit the tight access and sloped ground found around Wimberley. Our [brush clearing](brush-removal) work takes out the understory that hides a view, and [cedar removal](cedar-removal) thins the Ashe juniper competing with your oaks for water and light.

Everything gets ground down to a fine finish, the small chips some people call toothpicks. Root balls stay in the ground with mulching, so a Wimberley slope keeps its grip. A dozer working the same ground would disturb the soil and raise erosion risk.

sections.h2: Oak wilt and Wimberley live oaks
paras: Oak wilt is common in Central Texas, including the Hill Country around Wimberley. Texas A&M Forest Service explains that oak wilt moves underground through connected root systems, especially in live oaks, and through sap beetles that carry spores to fresh wounds.

Infected oaks cannot be restored, and the disease spreads in defined paths. When oak wilt is already on a Wimberley property, selective clearing is often the best way to protect the healthy trees around the infected ones.

sections.h2: Clearing near the water in Wimberley
paras: Ground along Cypress Creek and the Blanco River deserves extra care. Trees on a creek bank hold the soil when the water comes up, so leaving the bank trees standing and clearing brush on the higher ground is the safer plan.

Before any work near the water in Wimberley, check floodplain rules with the City of Wimberley or Hays County. Permitting questions near the creek belong with those offices. [Forestry mulching](forestry-mulching-and-land-clearing) itself keeps a light footprint, with no pushing, piling or burning.

faqs.q: When is it safe to trim or cut around oaks in Wimberley?
faqs.a: Texas A&M Forest Service advises avoiding pruning or wounding oaks in Wimberley and across Texas from February through June, when sap beetles spread oak wilt spores. Any wound on an oak should be painted immediately, in any season. Clearing near live oaks goes best with that calendar in mind.

faqs.q: Can you open a view on a Wimberley hillside without clearing it bare?
faqs.a: Yes. A view on a Wimberley hillside opens up with selective clearing that removes the cedar and understory blocking the line of sight and keeps the oaks framing it. Compact track machines handle the slope, and the fine mulch finish lets grass come back faster than chunky debris would.

faqs.q: What makes a Wimberley clearing job take longer?
faqs.a: A Wimberley clearing job takes longer when the work is selective, the slope is steep or access is tight. Picking around oaks goes slower than open acreage. Smaller machines clear about half an acre to 1 acre in an 8-hour day, and density and terrain change that pace.

faqs.q: Can you clear dead trees on a Wimberley property?
faqs.a: Yes. Drought stress and oak wilt both leave dead and declining trees across Central Texas, including around Wimberley. A forestry mulcher grinds dead standing trees and downed limbs in place, with no burn pile. Oaks infected with oak wilt cannot be restored, so removing them can help protect the healthy trees nearby.
